how_to_use: This is a local index, not a source of truth. Before relying on an entry, open its URL with the agent's web-fetch/browser tool and confirm the status, issue date, and whether a newer version supersedes it. A page that redirects to a generic landing page is usually archived.

entries.title: General Wellness: Policy for Low Risk Devices
entries.notes: Updated January 2026. Use for the wellness-vs-device boundary and for claims that stay unrelated to diagnosis, cure, mitigation, prevention, or treatment.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 01/06/2026'

entries.title: Policy for Device Software Functions and Mobile Medical Applications
entries.notes: Explains which software functions FDA does and does not intend to enforce against. A sleep app that only tracks or encourages healthy sleep may fall outside device oversight; claims to treat insomnia change the analysis.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 09/28/2022'

entries.title: Clinical Decision Support Software
entries.notes: Updated January 2026. Relevant if the product gives clinicians recommendations. The four 21st Century Cures Act criteria in FD&C Act 520(o)(1)(E) must all be met for non-device CDS.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 01/29/2026'

entries.title: Content of Premarket Submissions for Device Software Functions
entries.notes: Defines the Basic vs Enhanced software documentation level and the software lifecycle, verification, and validation content expected in a 510(k)/De Novo.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 06/14/2023'

entries.title: Cybersecurity in Medical Devices: Quality Management System Considerations and Content of Premarket Submissions
entries.notes: February 2026 version supersedes the June 2025 version. Covers section 524B 'cyber device' requirements, threat modeling, SBOM, vulnerability monitoring, and premarket documentation.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 02/03/2026'

entries.title: Marketing Submission Recommendations for a Predetermined Change Control Plan for Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions
entries.notes: Final August 2025. A PCCP can cover planned AI modifications; it is reviewed as part of the marketing submission and is not a blanket permission to change the intended use.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 08/18/2025'

entries.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions: Lifecycle Management and Marketing Submission Recommendations
entries.notes: Draft (90 FR 1154, 2025-01-07). As of 2026-10-23 no final FR notice was found; verify before treating any recommendation as final. Do not implement a draft as if it were binding.
entries.verified_via: federalregister.gov document opened 2026-10-23 (HTTP 200)

entries.title: Applying Human Factors and Usability Engineering to Medical Devices
entries.notes: Updated August 3, 2026 (originally February 2016). Patient-facing sleep apps need a use-related risk analysis and, where critical tasks exist, validation testing.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 08/03/2026'

entries.title: Content of Human Factors Information in Medical Device Marketing Submissions
entries.notes: Final May 29, 2026 (91 FR 32061); FDA indicated implementation beginning August 1, 2026. Sets three HF submission categories and the documentation for each.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 08/03/2026'

entries.title: Considerations for the Regulation of Generative AI-Enabled Medical Devices: Discussion Paper and Request for Feedback
entries.notes: August 18, 2026. Not draft or final guidance; does not represent policy. Useful for direction of travel (competency-based premarket evaluation, runtime governance) but do not cite as a requirement. Comment period closed 2026-10-19.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 08/18/2026'

entries.title: Software as a Medical Device (SaMD): Clinical Evaluation (FDA 2017; page appears archived)
entries.notes: FDA retired the original guidance page (it now redirects to the Digital Health Center of Excellence). The Federal Register notice of availability is the stable archival reference; FDA adoption was announced 2017-12-08, based on IMDRF/SaMD WG/N41.
entries.verified_via: FDA page redirects to the Digital Health Center of Excellence; Federal Register notice opened 2026-10-23 (HTTP 200)

entries.title: Off-the-Shelf Software Use in Medical Devices
entries.notes: Revised August 2023 (supersedes the September 2019 revision). Use for OTS software documentation expectations in a premarket submission.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; page dated August 2023, 'Content current as of: 08/11/2023'

entries.title: Deciding When to Submit a 510(k) for a Software Change to an Existing Device
entries.notes: Use for release planning: which changes need a new 510(k), which can be documented in the QMS, and how a PCCP changes the analysis. Live check required: this URL was not opened on 2026-10-23; confirm the page and status before citing.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 08/30/2018'

entries.title: Multiple Function Device Products: Policy and Considerations
entries.notes: When one product mixes device and non-device functions, FDA assesses the 'other functions' for their impact on the device function's safety and effectiveness. Use it when a sleep app combines wellness tracking with a treatment claim.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 07/28/2020'

entries.title: Design Considerations and Pre-market Submission Recommendations for Interoperable Medical Devices
entries.notes: Design and premarket recommendations for devices that exchange data (EHR, wearables, APIs): interface specification, verification, and labeling. Use when the app ingests wearable or EHR data.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 08/30/2018'

entries.title: General Principles of Software Validation
entries.notes: Still cited for software used in production or the QMS, and for V&V principles. It does not replace the 2023 premarket software content guidance for device software functions.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 05/15/2019'

entries.title: Postmarket Management of Cybersecurity in Medical Devices
entries.notes: Postmarket expectations: coordinated vulnerability disclosure, patch cadence, risk-based remediation, and 21 CFR 803/806 reporting. Complements the premarket cybersecurity guidance.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 10/01/2018'

entries.title: Requests for Feedback and Meetings for Medical Device Submissions: The Q-Submission Program
entries.notes: Pre-submission meetings and written feedback. Use before a 510(k)/De Novo to confirm intended use, predicate strategy, and test plans; a Q-Sub is not a clearance.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 05/28/2025'

entries.title: De Novo Classification Process (Evaluation of Automatic Class III Designation)
entries.notes: For a novel intended use with no valid predicate at low-to-moderate risk. A granted De Novo creates a new classification and product code, which later devices can use as a predicate.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 10/05/2021'

entries.title: FDA and Industry Procedures for Section 513(g) Requests for Information
entries.notes: FDA's written view on classification and applicable requirements (60-day response, user fee). Not a clearance, and not a substitute for a Q-Sub on test plans.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; page dated August 2024

entries.title: Medical Device Data Systems, Medical Image Storage Devices, and Medical Image Communications Devices
entries.notes: MDDS are Class I, 510(k)-exempt devices limited to storing/transmitting data. Active monitoring, analysis, or clinical decision support moves the product out of this exemption.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 09/28/2022'

entries.title: Breakthrough Devices Program
entries.notes: Expedited review for life-threatening or seriously debilitating conditions, with interactive review and prioritized resources. Optional, and it does not lower the evidence bar.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 09/14/2023'

entries.title: Medical Devices; Quality System Regulation Amendments (QMSR final rule)
entries.notes: 89 FR 7496. Effective February 2, 2026. 21 CFR Part 820 now incorporates ISO 13485:2016 by reference; the old QSR sections are gone. Technical amendments: 90 FR 55978 (2025-12-04).
entries.verified_via: federalregister.gov document opened 2026-10-23 (HTTP 200)

entries.title: 21 CFR Part 820 — Quality Management System Regulation
entries.notes: Use the eCFR API for the current text. Part 820 is now short because it incorporates ISO 13485 by reference.
entries.verified_via: ecfr.gov page opened 2026-10-23 (HTTP 200)

entries.title: 21 CFR 882.5801 — Computerized behavioral therapy device for psychiatric disorders
entries.notes: The QVO classification regulation. Class II, prescription only, adjunct to clinician-supervised outpatient treatment. Special controls require clinical data validating the behavioral therapy model and its implementation, plus software documentation.
entries.verified_via: ecfr.gov page opened 2026-10-23 (HTTP 200)

entries.title: 21 CFR 882.5705 — Digital therapy device to reduce sleep disturbance for psychiatric conditions
entries.notes: QMZ. Prescription device for sleep disturbance due to psychiatric conditions such as nightmare disorder or PTSD. Not a general insomnia code.
entries.verified_via: ecfr.gov page opened 2026-10-23 (HTTP 200)

entries.title: 21 CFR 882.5050 — Sleep assessment device
entries.notes: LEL. Class II sleep assessment devices (e.g., actigraphy). Relevant if the product measures sleep rather than treating insomnia.
entries.verified_via: ecfr.gov page opened 2026-10-23 (HTTP 200)

entries.title: 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart C — Security Rule
entries.notes: Administrative, physical, and technical safeguards (164.308, 164.310, 164.312), organizational requirements, and policies/procedures. The 2025 NPRM to strengthen the Security Rule is not final as of 2026-10-23.
entries.verified_via: ecfr.gov page opened 2026-10-23 (HTTP 200)

entries.title: HIPAA Security Rule To Strengthen the Cybersecurity of Electronic Protected Health Information
entries.notes: 90 FR 898. Proposed, not final as of 2026-10-23. Do not treat as binding, but use it as a design signal (asset inventory, encryption, MFA, contingency planning, 72-hour restoration).
entries.verified_via: federalregister.gov document opened 2026-10-23 (HTTP 200)

entries.title: 45 CFR 164.400-414 — Breach Notification Rule
entries.notes: Four-factor risk assessment, individual notice without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days, HHS notice, and media notice for 500+ residents of a state or jurisdiction.
entries.verified_via: ecfr.gov page opened 2026-10-23 (HTTP 200)

entries.title: Guidance on Risk Analysis Requirements under the HIPAA Security Rule
entries.notes: OCR's risk analysis guidance for 45 CFR 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A); the most common Security Rule audit finding. Covers scope, threats, likelihood, impact, and documentation.
entries.verified_via: hhs.gov page opened 2026-10-23; 'Content last reviewed August 12, 2026'

entries.title: Guidance on HIPAA and Cloud Computing
entries.notes: Cloud service providers are business associates even when they store only encrypted ePHI without a key; a BAA is required. Covers no-view services, SLAs, and cross-border storage.
entries.verified_via: hhs.gov page opened 2026-10-23; 'Content last reviewed December 23, 2022'

entries.title: 16 CFR Part 318 — Health Breach Notification Rule
entries.notes: 89 FR 47028. Applies to vendors of personal health records and related entities not covered by HIPAA. The FTC's 2024 amendments confirm that health apps can be covered. Check if the DTC app is outside HIPAA.
entries.verified_via: federalregister.gov document opened 2026-10-23 (HTTP 200)

entries.title: Health Products Compliance Guidance
entries.notes: Competent and reliable scientific evidence for health claims, including health apps. Use with the claims matrix; FTC applies to marketing that sits outside FDA labeling.
entries.verified_via: ftc.gov page opened 2026-10-23; title 'Health Products Compliance Guidance'

entries.title: IMDRF SaMD N10 — Key Definitions
entries.notes: Defines SaMD as software with a medical purpose that is not part of a hardware device, plus intended use and manufacturer terms. Read N10 before N12/N23/N41 so the vocabulary is stable.
entries.verified_via: imdrf.org page opened in browser 2026-10-23; page states 'Published date 18 December 2013'

entries.title: IMDRF SaMD N12 — Possible Framework for Risk Categorization and Corresponding Considerations
entries.notes: The four-category SaMD risk framework (I-III/IV) based on significance of the healthcare situation and the information provided. Useful for a defensible risk narrative, not a substitute for FDA classification.
entries.verified_via: imdrf.org page opened in browser 2026-10-23; page states 'Published date 18 September 2014'

entries.title: IMDRF SaMD N23 — Application of Quality Management System
entries.notes: Maps software lifecycle practices onto medical-device QMS expectations. Pairs with QMSR/ISO 13485 clause 7.3 when scoping design controls for a SaMD team.
entries.verified_via: imdrf.org page opened in browser 2026-10-23; page states 'Published date 2 October 2015'

entries.title: IMDRF SaMD N41 — Clinical Evaluation
entries.notes: Valid clinical association, analytical/technical validation, and clinical validation. This is the durable framework even though the FDA's 2017 adoption page appears archived.
entries.verified_via: imdrf.org page opened in browser 2026-10-23; page states 'Published date 21 September 2017'

entries.title: AASM Clinical Practice Guideline: Behavioral and Psychological Treatments for Chronic Insomnia Disorder in Adults
entries.notes: Strong recommendation for multicomponent CBT-I in adults. Sleep restriction has contraindications (high-risk occupations, mania/hypomania, poorly controlled seizures); single-component sleep hygiene is not recommended.
entries.verified_via: JCSM article opened 2026-10-23 (DOI 10.5664/jcsm.8986); published 2021-02

entries.title: FDA AI-Enabled Medical Device List
entries.notes: CSV download is available. The list is not comprehensive; use it for landscape scans and competitor/predicate discovery, then confirm each clearance in openFDA/accessdata.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 09/04/2026'

entries.title: FDA Recognized Consensus Standards Database
entries.notes: Check the recognition status and edition before citing ISO 13485, IEC 62304, ISO 14971, IEC 62366-1, or IEC 82304-1 in a submission.
entries.verified_via: accessdata.fda.gov search page opened 2026-10-23 (HTTP 200)

entries.title: NIST SP 800-66 Rev. 2 — Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule
entries.notes: Practical implementation guide for the Security Rule. Use it to structure the risk analysis and safeguard evidence, not as a legal safe harbor.
entries.verified_via: csrc.nist.gov page opened 2026-10-23 (HTTP 200)

entries.title: HHS 405(d) Health Industry Cybersecurity Practices (HICP) and Cyber Gateway
entries.notes: HICP (2023 edition) and the Cyber Gateway: implementation practices for the Security Rule. Use as evidence for safeguards, not as a binding standard.
entries.verified_via: 405d.hhs.gov opened 2026-10-23; page links 'HICP 2023'

entries.title: Guidances with Digital Health Content (FDA index)
entries.notes: Use this index to catch a guidance that is not in the local registry. It is updated more often than any static list. Live check required: this URL was not opened on 2026-10-23; confirm the page before citing.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 04/09/2026'

entries.title: Medical Device Software Guidance Navigator (FDA)
entries.notes: Interactive navigator for software-related guidance. Useful for a second pass after the local registry. Live check required: this URL was not opened on 2026-10-23; confirm the page before citing.
entries.verified_via: fda.gov page opened 2026-10-23; on-page 'Content current as of: 07/24/2025'

verification_policy: last_verified is the date the cited url was opened and checked. verified_via records what the page itself said (or the HTTP result). Re-verify an entry before changing its date; do not bulk-bump.
